title: Deep-Stats rows: per-bar statistics strip, configuration and export
body:
## Context
R2 "Order-flow beta" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §6) delivers DeepCharts-grade order-flow visibility. **E20 Deep-Stats rows** is the numeric layer of that: a configurable per-bar statistics strip under the chart that lets a trader read a bar without decoding footprint cells. Roadmap scope line (§6.2): "Configurable per-bar statistic rows under the chart: delta, cumulative delta, volume, buy/sell volume, trade count, average trade size, max/min delta, delta %, imbalance count, tape speed; row add/remove/reorder; per-row conditional highlighting; CSV export of the visible range" — 26 pts, Sprint S11, area `area/order-flow`, backend module **M9** (`orderflow`), story domain **DS**.

The numbers in the strip are **not a new calculation**. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 ("Deep Stats rows (per-bar statistics strip)") declares every row as a first-class `MetricDescriptor` in the `MetricRegistry` — `bar_volume`, `bar_notional`, `bar_buy_volume`, `bar_sell_volume`, `delta`, `max_delta`, `min_delta`, `delta_pct`, `bar_delta_divergence`, `cvd`, `cvd_bar_change`, `bar_trade_count`, `bar_avg_trade_size`, `bar_buy_trade_count`/`bar_sell_trade_count`, `tape_speed`, `bar_volume_imbalance_ratio`, `bar_poc_price`, `bar_vah_price`/`bar_val_price`, `open_interest_delta`, `bar_range_ticks` — all `scope="symbol"`, `cadence="on_trade"` with authoritative recompute `on_bar_close`, `inputs=("trades",)`, `deterministic=True`, `confidence="exact"`. The invariant this epic must protect is stated verbatim in that section: *a rule, an alert and a Deep-Stats row always read the same number*. There is therefore exactly one server-side engine — `DeepStatsEngine` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.4, fed by `FootprintEngine`) — and the strip is a renderer of its output, never a second implementation.

Depends on E18 Footprint (`E18 --> E20` in the roadmap dependency graph §11.1) for per-bar cell aggregation and the `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` WS topic, and on E16 Recorder for history depth. Consumes E11/E12 chart-engine surfaces for bar-grid alignment and E15 chart templates (`chart_templates`) for persistence of row configuration.

**Scheduling note (cross-epic blockers resolve strictly earlier).** Per the roadmap Gantt (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.2) E18 Footprint runs S10–S11 and E20 runs S11. E20 therefore never blocks on *all of* E18: each E20 ticket names the specific E18 child it consumes, and every such child is scheduled in a strictly earlier sprint than the E20 ticket that depends on it (E18-D02 S08 → E20-D01 S09; E18-T01/T02/T03/T04 and E18-S01/S02 S10 → E20-K01/T01/X01 S11). E18's own S11 work (display modes, imbalance zones, settings dialog, a11y) is *not* an input to E20.

**Estimate rollup (roadmap reconciliation).** Epic `estimate` = **26 pts**, matching the roadmap sizing for E20 exactly (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §6.2 E20 scope row and §5 epic table = 26). Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` the epic-level number is the **committed engineering rollup**: the in-train Story/Task/Spike children (S01 5, S02 3, S03 2, S04 3, T01 5, T02 2, T03 3, T04 1, K01 2) = 26 pts. The Could-have S05 (3 pts, Backlog) is excluded because it is not committed to the train, and the Design (D01–D06, 14 pts), QA (Q01–Q05, 12 pts) and Security (X01–X02, 4 pts) children are tracked as discipline overhead against the design/QA/security capacity lines rather than the epic's feature sizing — counting them was what produced the stale 59 and a ~127% overshoot of the roadmap figure. 26 vs 26 is 0% variance, inside the ±15% tolerance band.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Stories:** US-DS-001 (Must, per-bar statistics strip), US-DS-002 (Must, row selection & ordering), US-DS-003 (Should, threshold colouring), US-DS-005 (Should, stats export + accessible table), US-DS-004 (Could, rolling sparkline — Backlog, ship only if capacity allows).
- **Screens:** SCR-030 Chart panel (hosts the strip), SCR-033 Deep Stats rows configuration (new modal), SCR-045 Chart data-table alternative (a11y + CSV export).
- **Components:** CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip (new organism), consuming CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-031 ColorSwatch/ThemeChip, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-049 Table, CMP-053 Pagination, CMP-056 ColumnPicker, CMP-099 PrintExportBar.
- **Backend (M9):** `DeepStatsEngine` emitting `DeepStatsRow`; registration of every §7 Deep-Stats `MetricDescriptor` in `MetricRegistry`; chunked CSV export job.
- **Contracts:** `GET /market/metrics` (repeatable `metric`, bar-scoped), `GET /market/footprint` bootstrap, WS topic `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` (§14.4 `FootprintUpdate` — per-bar `delta`, `poc_price`, `value_area_high/low`), export job polled via `GET /jobs/{id}`.
- **DB:** `chart_templates` jsonb config (row set/order/format/thresholds), `layout_panes.pane_kind = 'deep_stats'`, QuestDB `footprint_cells` + `trades` read-side, Parquet cold tier for offline parity recompute.
- **Analytics/audit:** `chart.deepstats_rows_changed {rows}`, `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported`.
- Design track D01–D06, QA track Q01–Q05, Security track X01–X02, ADR + docs T04.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell rendering (E18), profiles (E19), CVD pane and divergence markers (E23), tape-speed detector internals and z-score baselining (E25), OI/funding series (E24) — E20 only *displays* `tape_speed` and `open_interest_delta` by reading their registered descriptors.
- Alerting or rule authoring on a stats row (E40 / E35). The shared `MetricRegistry` makes this trivial later; no rule surface is built here.
- Android / any mobile client (owner decision 2026-09-14); no separate admin app.
- Non-Bybit venues; anything other than Bybit USDT linear perpetuals.
- Multi-symbol comparison of stats rows (E23 owns multi-symbol CVD comparison).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The strip reads the market
  Given a recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day is loaded on SCR-030 with the Deep Stats strip enabled
  When the user scrolls and zooms across the visible range
  Then every enabled row is pixel-aligned with its bar column at every zoom level
  And the forming bar is rendered in the documented provisional style
  And the strip costs <= 1.5 ms per frame measured over a 60-second capture

Scenario: One number everywhere
  Given the offline DuckDB recomputation over the Parquet tier for the same symbol-day
  When each Deep-Stats row value is compared with the value served by GET /market/metrics and the value rendered in the strip
  Then all three agree within floating-point tolerance for 100% of bars
  And every row label maps to a registered MetricDescriptor, asserted by the CI test required by 24-internal-schemas.md §12

Scenario: Configuration survives and is reachable without a mouse
  Given the user disables Max Delta and Min Delta and moves Cumulative Delta to the top using Alt+Up
  When the workspace is reloaded
  Then the row set and order are restored from the chart template
  And SCR-033, the strip and SCR-045 all pass axe-core with zero serious or critical violations

Scenario: Export is honest and bounded
  Given a visible range of 60 000 bars
  When the user exports the strip as CSV
  Then the export is chunked with visible progress and can be cancelled
  And the produced file has one row per bar, one column per enabled statistic and ISO-8601 UTC timestamps
  And a viewer-role user can export only the data their role can see

Scenario: Partial history is never silently truncated
  Given the recorder started 4 minutes ago for SOLUSDT
  When the strip is enabled on a 5m chart
  Then a partial-history state is shown naming the first available timestamp
  And rows that cannot be computed for the uncovered bars render as explicit "no data", not as zero
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Engine.** `DeepStatsEngine` (`20-architecture.md` §3.4) is incremental and checkpointable: it consumes `FootprintUpdate` plus the raw trade stream for the forming bar, maintains per-bar accumulators (`buy_volume`, `sell_volume`, running delta with `max_delta`/`min_delta` path tracking, trade counts by aggressor, notional), and emits `DeepStatsRow` on the coalescing `of.*` bus. Values are re-derived authoritatively `on_bar_close`; the in-progress bar is provisional, coalesced to 4 Hz (CMP-225 data contract).
- **No second maths in the browser.** The frontend renders values from the WS frame / REST bootstrap and never recomputes a statistic. The only frontend-derived quantity permitted is the sparkline window, which is a windowing of already-delivered values.
- **Alignment.** The strip is a real `<table>` (CMP-225 a11y contract) positioned from the engine's time-scale projection `x(t)`, the same one CMP-181 CandleSeries uses, so alignment cannot drift.
- **Recompute cadence.** Per SCR-033 Performance: recomputed on bar close and on visible-range change, not per tick.
- **Config persistence.** Row ids, order, per-row format, threshold rules and compact/sparkline flags live in `chart_templates` jsonb (`21-database-schema.md` §3.8.2) so they travel with the template; `layout_panes.pane_kind='deep_stats'` covers the standalone-pane case.
- **Error codes.** Reuse the documented `validation_failed` and `footprint_window_too_large`; add no new error family.

## Test plan
- Unit: per-metric golden tests for all §7 descriptors; accumulator edge cases (zero-volume bar, single-print bar, `qty_step` divide guard in `delta_pct`).
- Contract: OpenAPI + WS JSON-schema validation for every consumed frame shape.
- Integration: recorded Bybit fixtures — normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol (R2 §6.4 gate list).
- Golden fixture: version-controlled expected Deep-Stats output for one recorded symbol-day; drift fails CI (R2 correctness gate).
- E2E (Playwright web + Electron): enable strip, toggle/reorder rows, thresholds, table view, CSV export including cancel.
- Perf: strip frame-cost benchmark in CI (<=1.5 ms/frame) plus a full-scene budget re-check (footprint + profile + heatmap + bubbles + 3 stat rows + CVD, p95 <=16.6 ms).
- A11y: axe-core CI on SCR-033/SCR-045 plus a manual screen-reader pass over the strip table and keyboard reorder.
- Coverage: >=85% backend/engine packages, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Data classification: market data only — no PII, no secrets, no order or credential surface. Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **S4 information disclosure via export** (SR-098 — exports role-scoped, watermarked with the exporting identity and timestamp, and audited), **S3 path handling on export** (SR-097 — no user-supplied filesystem paths; downloads addressed by job id through `GET /jobs/{id}`), and a denial-of-service vector from unbounded export ranges (chunking plus a hard cap). The read path is gated by `marketdata:read` with `scope=none` (`23-ws-protocol.md` subscription permission table). Epic carries the `security` label; STRIDE is E20-X01.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. The strip is a real table, not canvas, so values are readable cell by cell; drag reorder has the `Alt+Up`/`Alt+Down` keyboard equivalent (SCR-033); threshold state is conveyed by a word plus an icon — **never colour alone** (US-DS-003 NFR); SCR-045 is the normative accessible equivalent and must reach reading parity; a documented "read current bar's stats" shortcut exists (CMP-225).

## Performance notes
Budgets from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: frame budget #1 (p95 <=16.6 ms), floor #2 (never below 30 fps) for the full R2 scene, and WS tick -> screen #3 (p95 <100 ms, hard gate at R2). Epic-specific: the strip adds <=2 ms/frame (US-DS-001 NFR) with the tighter screen-level budget of <=1.5 ms/frame (SCR-033). The virtualised SCR-045 table renders 100k rows at <=8 ms scripting per scroll frame.

## Observability
Structured logs for export jobs (job id, range, bar count, duration, outcome); Prometheus metrics `deepstats_engine_bar_close_duration_seconds`, `deepstats_rows_emitted_total`, `deepstats_export_rows_total`, `deepstats_export_failures_total`; frontend strip frame cost surfaced in the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay; analytics events `chart.deepstats_rows_changed`, `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported`; export audited per SR-098.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 (Epic):
- [ ] Epic `estimate` (26) still reconciles with the roadmap E20 sizing (26) within ±15%, and with the in-train S/T/K child sum, at each sprint boundary.
- [ ] No child ticket scheduled in a sprint earlier than any of its cross-epic blockers' sprints (re-checked whenever the roadmap Gantt moves).
- [ ] All child Stories/Tasks/Spikes/Design/QA/Security tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition (US-DS-004 is the expected descope candidate).
- [ ] Epic-level acceptance criteria above verified end-to-end on a recorded symbol-day.
- [ ] Coverage floors green (>=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend); zero open P0/P1 against E20 scope.
- [ ] Docs updated: `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 row table, `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-033/SCR-045, `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-225, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md` for any shipped delta.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green plus manual screen-reader pass recorded (E20-Q04).
- [ ] perf: strip frame-cost benchmark recorded against budget (E20-Q03).
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off (E20-X01/X02).
- [ ] QA sign-off: epic-level regression and exploratory pass recorded (E20-Q05).
- [ ] Design sign-off: design-QA sweep Done (E20-D06).
- [ ] Demoed to Owner at Sprint Review with acceptance recorded; ADR-0016 merged (E20-T04).

## Dependencies
- **E18 Footprint** (S10–S11) — E20 consumes only E18's **Sprint 10** deliverables: `E18-T01`/`E18-T02` (cell aggregation + imbalance/POC/value-area algorithms) feed `DeepStatsEngine`; `E18-T03`/`E18-T04` (REST + WS footprint read paths) define the surface E20-X01 threat-models and E20-T02 extends; `E18-S01`/`E18-S02` (cell grid render) give E20-K01 a real scene to measure; `E18-D02` (S08) is the stimulus for E20-D01. Each E20 child names the specific earlier-sprint child it needs, so no E20 ticket is scheduled before its blocker resolves. E18's Sprint-11 work is not an input to E20.

- **E11 / E12** — engine time-scale projection and bar series used for alignment.

- **E05 design system** — CMP-008/024/031/043/049/053/056/099 must exist before CMP-225 is composed.

title: UX research: how traders read per-bar statistics
body:
## Context
E20 introduces one net-new modal (SCR-033 Deep Stats rows configuration) and one net-new organism (CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip) that sits permanently under the chart consuming vertical space the trader would otherwise give to price. The catalogue in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 offers **21 possible rows**; SCR-033's wireframe shows 13. Which rows a trader actually wants by default, how many they will tolerate before the strip stops paying for its height, and whether they read the strip or the footprint cells first are empirical questions. US-DS-002 exists precisely because "the strip fits my screen budget" is a real constraint. This ticket produces the evidence the wireframes (E20-D02) are argued from, two sprints ahead of the consuming FE story (E20-S01, Sprint 11) per the design-ahead rule.

The stimulus for the probe is the E18-D02 footprint wireframe set (Sprint 08), not a running footprint build — this keeps the whole S09 design track startable ahead of E18's S10–S11 engineering window.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3–4 moderated sessions (Owner + up to 2 account managers + 1 proxy order-flow trader), 45 min each, screen-shared against their current DeepCharts/ATAS/Sierra setup.
- Task-based probes: read the last bar's aggression without touching the footprint; find the bar with the largest delta in the visible range; decide whether a bar is "strong" from the numbers alone; configure a strip for a 1-minute scalping session vs a 15-minute swing session.
- Row-ranking exercise over the full 21-row catalogue from `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 (card sort): produces an ordered list and a defensible **default row set** (target: 4–6 rows) plus a defensible **compact-mode row set**.
- Evidence on threshold semantics for US-DS-003: what "significant" means numerically for delta %, and whether thresholds are per-symbol in practice (the story asserts they are — confirm or refute).
- Competitive teardown of stats strips (DeepCharts "Deep Stats"/On-Candle Stats, ATAS, Sierra Chart) covering row catalogues, compact modes, alignment behaviour at narrow bar widths, and threshold highlighting conventions.
- Findings written to `docs/design/research/e20-deep-stats.md`: ranked row frequencies, the recommended default and compact row sets, vocabulary for row labels (must reconcile with the UI labels fixed in §7 — deviations flagged as doc changes, not silent renames), and 5–8 adopted design decisions each phrased as a testable statement.

## Out of scope
- Any visual design — greyscale wireframes start in E20-D02.
- Footprint cell research (E18), profile research (E19), DOM ladder research (E21).
- Recruiting participants outside the owner's circle.
- Deciding the sparkline (US-DS-004) feature's existence — it is a Could; research may report on it but does not gate it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Default row set is evidence-backed
  When docs/design/research/e20-deep-stats.md is reviewed
  Then it names a default row set of 4-6 rows with the session evidence for each inclusion
  And every named row maps to a MetricDescriptor listed in 24-internal-schemas.md §7

Scenario: Narrow-bar behaviour has a decided answer
  Given US-DS-001 requires a compact form below a minimum legible bar width
  When the findings are reviewed
  Then they state what traders expect to see in that compact form and what they expect to read in the crosshair readout instead

Scenario: Threshold assumption tested
  When the threshold probe results are reviewed
  Then the per-symbol-thresholds assumption in US-DS-003 is either confirmed with evidence or explicitly refuted with a recorded recommendation to change the story
```

## Technical notes / design
Sessions are recorded (with consent) and stored under `docs/design/research/raw/e20/`. Card sort uses the exact row labels from `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 so results are directly actionable. No prototype is built; probes run against the participants' existing tools and the R1 chart build.

## Test plan
N/A (research ticket). Verification is the artefact review in the acceptance criteria, performed by the CDO and the E20 engineering lead.

## Security notes
Session recordings may capture participants' own account balances and positions on their existing tooling. Recordings must be stored access-restricted and redacted before any excerpt is shared; no credentials are ever entered during a session. Data classification: internal. No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
At least one probe is run keyboard-only to gather evidence on how a non-mouse user would reorder rows, feeding the `Alt+Up`/`Alt+Down` requirement in SCR-033.

## Performance notes
N/A — no code produced. Research does surface the perceived cost ceiling ("how many rows before this feels heavy"), which E20-K01 then measures for real.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2 (Task):
- [ ] `docs/design/research/e20-deep-stats.md` merged with ranked rows, default + compact sets, and 5–8 testable design decisions.
- [ ] Acceptance criteria above verified in an artefact review by the CDO and the E20 engineering lead.
- [ ] Any recommended change to US-DS-002/US-DS-003 raised as a doc PR against `11-user-stories.md` rather than left in the research file.
- [ ] Findings presented at the design review; E20-D02 unblocked.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E18-D02` (*Wireframe the footprint layer on SCR-030, SCR-032 and the SCR-056 imbalance surfaces*, Sprint 08) — participants must be able to see a concrete footprint rendering to answer "do you read the strip or the cells first"; the E18 wireframes plus the E18-D01 research prototype are sufficient stimulus, and they land a full sprint before this ticket starts.

This deliberately does **not** block on the E18 epic as a whole: E18 runs S10–S11 per the roadmap Gantt (`30-release-roadmap.md` §11.2), so an `E18` epic-level blocker would make this Sprint-09 ticket unstartable and would cascade the same violation onto E20-D02/D03. Footprint *rendering* is not required for a research probe; footprint *wireframes* are. The downstream design chain (D02 S09 → D03 S09 → D04/D05 S10) therefore inherits only the S08 dependency and is schedulable in-window, preserving the design-ahead rule for the Sprint-11 stories.

## Context
Hi-fi visual design for the E20 surfaces, and the design-system contribution that makes **CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip** a first-class catalogue organism rather than a one-off. ## Scope / Deliverables

- Provisional (forming-bar) treatment: a documented, non-colour-only encoding distinguishing the in-progress bar's values.

- Redlines: spacing, row height at both densities, alignment rules against the bar grid, focus rings.

## Out of scope


All values come from tokens; no raw hex. Row height must be expressible as a whole number of `space.1` units at both densities so the strip's total height is predictable for the layout engine. Focus rings, hit targets (>=24×24 CSS px per WCAG 2.2 AA target-size), threshold word+glyph pairs, and the visible keyboard-reorder affordance are all specified with redlines. The strip's table semantics are re-affirmed in the spec so it is not implemented as canvas.

The spec must not require per-cell effects (shadows, gradients, blurs) that would push the strip past its <=1.5 ms/frame budget; any such effect is called out and justified or removed.

title: Motion spec and accessibility review for the Deep-Stats strip
body:
## Context
The strip updates continuously — the forming bar's values change up to 4 Hz (CMP-225 data contract) — while sitting in the trader's peripheral vision next to a live chart. Unspecified motion here is actively harmful: value flicker reads as noise and, for a screen-reader user, an unguarded live region would flood output. This ticket fixes the motion language and runs the formal accessibility review of the E20 designs before engineering starts in Sprint 11.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Motion spec** (`docs/design/e20-motion.md` + Figma prototype): value-change transition (duration, easing, and the explicit decision on whether a changing value animates at all at 4 Hz — the default position is that it does not, and the spec must argue whichever way it lands); row add/remove and reorder transitions in SCR-033 and in the strip; threshold-breach entry/exit; strip show/hide; export progress. Every duration/easing expressed as a token from `16-design-system-brief.md`.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour** for every motion above, specified as a complete alternative, not "animation off".
- **Accessibility review** of the full E20 design set against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: table semantics and header association for the strip; the accessible name of every SCR-033 control; the keyboard reorder contract (`Alt+Up`/`Alt+Down`) including the announcement made after a move ("Cumulative Delta moved to position 1 of 5"); the "read current bar's stats" shortcut's announcement text; live-region policy for the forming bar (must default to non-announcing, opt-in only, mirroring the CMP-226 BarCountdown precedent); focus management on modal open/close and after the export completes.
- A written a11y acceptance checklist that E20-Q04 executes verbatim.

## Out of scope
- Implementation of any of it (E20-S01..S04).
- Motion for the chart canvas, footprint cells or heatmap (E18/E21).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reduced motion is a designed alternative
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  When the motion spec is reviewed
  Then every animated behaviour has a specified non-animated equivalent that still communicates the same change

Scenario: The forming bar does not flood a screen reader
  When the live-region policy is reviewed
  Then the forming bar's values are non-announcing by default and announcement is opt-in, with the opt-in control named

Scenario: Reorder is announced
  When a row is moved with Alt+Up
  Then the spec defines the exact announcement string including the new position and the total count
```

## Technical notes / design
Motion tokens only. The 4 Hz coalescing cadence is the hard constraint: any transition longer than ~250 ms would still be running when the next value arrives, which is the technical argument the spec must engage with. Announcement strings are specified as i18n-ready message templates even though v1 ships English only.

## Test plan

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility review. Sign-off by the accessibility specialist is mandatory and is a gate on E20-D05 handoff.

## Performance notes
Motion choices are bounded by the strip's <=1.5 ms/frame budget; any transition requiring per-frame layout work is rejected in favour of compositor-only properties.

title: Measure strip frame cost and bar-grid alignment strategy
body:
## Context
SCR-033 sets a hard screen-level budget: "The Deep Stats strip is recomputed only on bar close and on the visible-range change, not per tick; it must add <=1.5 ms per frame to the chart panel's budget." US-DS-001's NFR is slightly looser (<=2 ms) and adds an absolute requirement: "alignment is pixel-exact with the bar grid at all zoom levels". Those two requirements pull against each other, because the cheapest way to guarantee alignment is to render the strip inside the WebGL pass (one projection, one frame), while the a11y contract in `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-225 mandates the opposite — "rendered as a real `<table>` aligned to the bar grid (not canvas), so values are readable cell by cell". US-DS-004 then asserts sparklines are "drawn in the same WebGL pass as the strip", implying a hybrid. This spike settles the architecture before E20-S01 commits to it, and measures the actual cost so E20-D03's density decisions are bounded by evidence rather than taste.

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. Not expected to produce production-shippable code.

## Scope / Deliverables
Questions to answer, each with recorded numbers:
1. **Can a DOM `<table>` of N columns × M rows stay pixel-aligned with the WebGL bar grid during pan/zoom without lagging a frame?** Measure at M = 5 and M = 13 rows, N = the visible bar count at 3 zoom levels (typical ~120 bars, dense ~400 bars, extreme ~800 bars).
2. **What does it cost?** Scripting + layout + paint time per frame attributable to the strip, p50/p95 over a 60 s pan/zoom capture, on the reference machine from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3, in Chromium and in the Electron shell.
3. **At what bar width does the strip stop being legible**, fixing the narrow-bar collapse threshold that US-DS-001 requires and E20-D05's measurement contract publishes.
4. **Which alignment strategy wins**: (a) per-cell absolutely-positioned DOM driven by the engine's `x(t)` each frame; (b) a single CSS transform on a fixed-pitch table, with the engine supplying scale + offset; (c) hybrid — WebGL-drawn backgrounds/sparklines with a DOM text layer on top. Compare on cost, alignment exactness and a11y fidelity.
5. **Does the 4 Hz coalesced forming-bar update cause layout thrash**, and does batching updates to `requestAnimationFrame` remove it?

Deliverables: prototype on `spike/e20-strip-alignment` (throwaway), a comparison table of the three strategies against the five questions, a Chrome DevTools performance trace per strategy committed under `docs/plan/benchmarks/e20/`, and a recommendation.

## Out of scope
- Any production implementation, styling, or real data plumbing — synthetic data is sufficient.
- Sparkline rendering cost beyond a rough feasibility note (US-DS-004 is a Could).
- Tauri measurement (E11's shell spike owns shell parity).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The architecture question is decided with evidence
  When the spike report is reviewed
  Then one of the three alignment strategies is recommended with measured p50/p95 frame cost for each at 5 and 13 rows
  And the recommendation states which strategy keeps the a11y table contract intact

Scenario: The budget is shown to be reachable or not
  When the recommended strategy's numbers are reviewed
  Then the report states whether <=1.5 ms per frame holds at 13 rows and 400 visible bars
  And if it does not, it states the maximum row count at which it does hold

Scenario: The collapse threshold is a number
  When the legibility measurement is reviewed
  Then a specific bar width in CSS pixels is named as the compact-collapse threshold, with the density and font size it was measured at
```

## Technical notes / design
Prototype against the E18 build so the strip is measured with a real footprint scene underneath it, not in isolation — the budget that matters is the marginal cost added to an already-loaded frame. Use `performance.measure` around the strip's update path and attribute layout/paint via the DevTools trace rather than wall-clock timers alone. Reference hardware and measurement method per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3 and §7.

## Test plan
The spike's output *is* measurement. Each number is reproduced at least twice; medians reported. The harness is retained (even though the prototype is throwaway) and promoted into the CI benchmark in E20-Q03.

## Security notes
N/A — synthetic data, no network, no credentials, throwaway branch not merged.

## Accessibility notes
A11y fidelity is an explicit comparison axis: any strategy that breaks the "real `<table>`, readable cell by cell" contract from CMP-225 is disqualified unless it provides an equivalent DOM mirror, and the report must say so explicitly.

## Performance notes
Budgets under test: SCR-033 <=1.5 ms/frame (screen-level), US-DS-001 <=2 ms/frame (story NFR), and `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budget #1 (frame p95 <=16.6 ms) / #2 (never below 30 fps) for the combined scene.

## Observability
The instrumentation added for the spike (a named `performance.measure` around the strip update) is specified for retention in the production implementation so SCR-046's diagnostics overlay can display strip frame cost.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2 (Spike):
- [ ] All five questions answered with recorded evidence; comparison table and traces committed under `docs/plan/benchmarks/e20/`.
- [ ] Decision recorded in **ADR-0016** (created by E20-T04, which references this spike's findings).
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed or updated: E20-S01's technical notes amended with the chosen strategy; E20-D03/E20-D05 given the collapse threshold and the affordable row count.
- [ ] Spike branch left unmerged and marked throwaway; the benchmark harness extracted into the E20-Q03 ticket.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review; `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new render-performance risk surfaced.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E18-S01` (*Render the footprint cell grid with tick aggregation and text LOD*, Sprint 10) and `E18-S02` (*bid/ask split cells with narrow-cell degradation*, Sprint 10) — the marginal frame cost of the strip is only meaningful measured on top of a real footprint scene at realistic cell density.

Scheduled **Sprint 11**, strictly after both blockers' sprint: the previous `blocked_by: E18` (epic, S10–S11) on a Sprint-10 spike would have measured against a scene that did not yet render. E18's remaining S11 stories change cell *appearance*, not cell *count*, so they do not move the measured budget materially; if the S11 imbalance-zone work (E18-S08) lands after this spike and changes draw-call counts, E20-Q03 (Sprint 12) re-measures against the final scene and is the gate of record. The spike must complete early in Sprint 11 because E20-S01 consumes its verdict.

`spike/e20-strip-alignment` — throwaway; only `docs/plan/benchmarks/e20/*` is merged.

body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` places E2E (Playwright, web + Electron) at the top of the pyramid, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires each story's acceptance scenarios to be demonstrated by an automated test referencing the specific scenario. This ticket automates the durable parts of the E20-Q01 plan so the strip is protected against regression for the rest of the programme — particularly through R3, when the chart panel gains trading overlays that will compete with the strip for the same space and the same frame budget.

## Scope / Deliverables
Playwright specs under `e2e/e20/`, each test named for the story scenario it demonstrates:
- **Strip (US-DS-001)**: rows render and align (bounding-box assertions against the canvas bar positions at 3 zoom levels); forming bar is provisional then replaced on close; narrow-bar collapse and crosshair readout; partial-history state naming the first available timestamp; "no data" rather than zero before recording start.
- **Configuration (US-DS-002)**: toggle rows and observe the height change; drag reorder; `Alt+Up`/`Alt+Down` keyboard reorder with the announcement asserted from the accessibility tree; reload and assert restoration; all-rows-off hides the strip and the restore affordance works; unavailable source listed and not enableable.
- **Thresholds (US-DS-003)**: configure a threshold, observe a breach on a known fixture bar, assert both the glyph and the accessible-name word are present; per-symbol sets applied on symbol switch with the set named in the legend; thresholds off returns everything to neutral; invalid input refused with the message.
- **Table and export (US-DS-005)**: `Alt+T` opens the table; keyboard-only navigation and `Enter` expansion; `Ctrl+C` TSV copy; small-range CSV export with content assertions (one row per bar, one column per statistic, ISO-8601 UTC, watermark present); large-range chunked export with progress and a cancel that leaves no downloadable artefact; insufficient-role export state.
- **Replay parity**: the same recorded window rendered live and through replay produces an identical strip state (R2 exit criterion #1 — "one shared pipeline used identically by live and replay").
- Runs in **both** the web and Electron targets, as the testing strategy requires.
- Deterministic fixtures: all specs run against recorded Bybit fixtures with a pinned clock, so no test depends on live market conditions.

## Out of scope
- Perf benchmarking (E20-Q03), a11y audit (E20-Q04), security testing (E20-X02) — each has its own ticket, though the E2E suite asserts the *presence* of a11y attributes where that is cheap.
- Backend unit or contract tests (owned by E20-T01/T02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  When the suite is cross-checked against US-DS-001, US-DS-002, US-DS-003 and US-DS-005
  Then every Gherkin scenario has a named E2E test, or a documented exception with a manual test-plan step and an automation follow-up ticket

Scenario: The suite is deterministic
  Given the suite is run 10 times against the same fixtures
  Then it passes 10 times with no flake
  And no test depends on wall-clock time or live market data

Scenario: Both shells are covered
  When the suite runs in CI
  Then it executes against both the web and the Electron targets

Scenario: Replay and live agree
  When the same recorded window is rendered live and through replay
  Then the asserted strip state is identical
```

## Technical notes / design
- Alignment assertions compare the strip cell's bounding box against the canvas bar's x-position exposed by a test-only engine hook; without that hook the test would be reduced to a screenshot comparison, which is flakier and less diagnostic.
- The accessibility-tree assertions use Playwright's accessibility snapshot so the reorder announcement and the threshold word are verified as they are actually exposed, not as they are intended.
- Export content assertions parse the CSV rather than matching a byte string, so a benign column-order change does not fail the suite while a wrong value does.
- Suite runtime budget: <=8 minutes so it can gate PRs touching E20 surfaces.

## Test plan
Meta: the suite's own reliability is verified by the 10× run in the acceptance criteria, and by deliberately breaking each asserted behaviour once to confirm the corresponding test fails (a test that cannot fail is not a test).

## Security notes
Includes the black-box security cases from E20-Q01: viewer-role export refusal and the cancelled-export-leaves-no-artefact assertion. Test fixtures contain market data only; no credentials are committed, and the test user accounts are provisioned by the existing E2E harness.

## Accessibility notes
The suite asserts the presence and content of the accessibility tree for the strip table, the reorder announcement and the threshold state word. It does not replace the manual audit (E20-Q04) but it prevents silent regression of the attributes that audit will check.

## Performance notes
Suite runtime <=8 minutes. The E2E suite deliberately does not assert frame timings — E20-Q03's dedicated benchmark does, because timing assertions in an E2E runner are a well-known flake source.

## Observability
CI publishes traces and videos for failures, retained per the CI policy, so a failure in the strip's alignment is diagnosable without local reproduction.

title: Performance benchmark and load profile for the Deep-Stats strip
body:
## Context
R2's exit criterion #2 is a hard gate: "Frame budget holds with the *full* order-flow scene: footprint + profile + heatmap + bubbles + **3 stat rows** + CVD pane, p95 <=16.6 ms; worst case never below 30 fps." The Deep-Stats strip is explicitly part of that scene. SCR-033 sets the strip's own allocation at <=1.5 ms/frame and US-DS-001 at <=2 ms. `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §8 requires a CI regression gate for every budget. This ticket turns E20-K01's throwaway measurement harness into that permanent gate.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A CI benchmark measuring the strip's marginal frame cost (scripting + layout + paint attributable to the strip) at p50/p95 over a scripted 60-second pan/zoom/live-update capture, run on the reference hardware profile from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.
- Configurations benchmarked: 3 rows (the R2 scene configuration), 9 rows (the US-DS-001 default set), 13 rows (the full SCR-033 catalogue), each at typical (~120), dense (~400) and extreme (~800) visible bars, with thresholds enabled — because thresholds enabled is the configuration users actually run.
- A **full-scene** benchmark run: footprint + profile + heatmap + bubbles + 3 stat rows + CVD pane together, asserting overall frame p95 <=16.6 ms and the 30 fps floor, coordinated with E18/E19/E21/E23's benchmarks so the scene is assembled once rather than four times.
- **WS tick → screen** measurement for a Deep-Stats value under the heaviest topic set, against budget #3 (p95 <100 ms, hard gate at R2).
- Virtualised-table scroll benchmark for SCR-045: <=8 ms scripting per scroll frame at 100k rows.
- A **load profile** exercising the strip under a sustained high-message-rate fixture (high-volatility burst) for 10 minutes, asserting no unbounded memory growth on the client and no coalescing backlog.
- Regression gate wired into CI with a documented allowed-variance threshold and a recorded baseline; a regression beyond it fails the build with the before/after numbers.
- Results published to `docs/plan/benchmarks/e20/` with the hardware profile, build SHA and date recorded per measurement.

## Out of scope
- Optimisation work — this ticket measures and gates; fixes are filed as Bugs or handled in the implementing stories.
- Backend ingestion soak (owned by the R2 load gate) and k6/Locust API load (owned by the API perf tickets), except for the WS tick → screen measurement above.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The strip's own budget is measured and gated
  When the benchmark runs at 9 rows and 400 visible bars with thresholds enabled
  Then the strip's marginal frame cost p95 is recorded
  And CI fails if it exceeds 1.5 ms beyond the allowed variance

Scenario: The full R2 scene holds
  Given footprint, profile, heatmap, bubbles, 3 stat rows and the CVD pane are all rendered
  Then frame p95 is <= 16.6 ms
  And the measured frame rate never falls below 30 fps during the capture

Scenario: Tick to screen holds under the heaviest topic set
  When a Deep-Stats value change is timed from WS receipt to paint
  Then p95 is < 100 ms

Scenario: No leak under sustained load
  Given the high-volatility fixture is replayed for 10 minutes
  Then client memory attributable to the strip is flat within the documented tolerance
  And no coalescing backlog accumulates

Scenario: A regression is caught, not absorbed
  Given a deliberate 1 ms regression is introduced into the strip update path
  Then the CI gate fails and reports the before and after numbers
```

## Technical notes / design
- Measurement method follows `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7: DevTools trace attribution rather than wall-clock timers alone, medians of repeated runs, and the reference hardware profile stated with every number.

## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI and manual screen-reader passes; R2's a11y quality gate additionally requires colour-blind-safe verification of the green/red conventions and non-colour alternatives throughout. E20 has three surfaces that matter disproportionately here: the strip is the numeric layer that makes the canvas readable at all, **SCR-045 is the normative accessible equivalent of the whole chart** ("must reach feature parity for reading data; verified in every a11y test pass"), and SCR-033 is a drag-reorder interface, historically the most common place keyboard equivalence is promised and not delivered. This is the formal audit against the checklist E20-D04 produced.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Execute the `docs/design/e20-a11y-checklist.md` checklist from E20-D04 verbatim against the built surfaces, recording pass/fail per item.
- **Automated**: axe-core runs on SCR-030 with the strip enabled, SCR-033 and SCR-045, in light and dark themes at both densities — zero serious or critical violations required, all moderate/minor triaged.
- **Manual screen-reader passes** with at least two combinations from the standard's supported matrix (e.g. NVDA + Chromium, VoiceOver + WebKit/Electron): read the strip cell by cell; confirm row headers name each statistic and its unit; confirm the forming bar does not announce unless opted in; execute the "read current bar's stats" shortcut; perform a keyboard reorder and verify the announcement string matches the spec exactly; open and dismiss SCR-033 verifying focus management; navigate SCR-045 by keyboard, expand a bar, copy as TSV, run an export and verify progress and completion are announced politely.
- **Keyboard-only pass**: every E20 action performed with no pointer, including reorder, threshold entry, table navigation and export — with no keyboard trap and visible focus throughout.
- **Colour-independence verification**: greyscale and deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia simulations of the threshold states, the provisional forming-bar treatment and the unavailable-row state; each must remain distinguishable.
- **Contrast measurement** of all strip text, threshold shades and focus indicators in both themes at both densities.
- **Reading-parity verification**: a documented comparison confirming every value visible in the strip is obtainable from SCR-045 for the same range.
- Findings logged as Bugs with severity and WCAG success-criterion references; blockers fixed before sign-off.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the findings (filed as Bugs against the implementing stories), except trivial attribute fixes agreed inline.

```gherkin
Scenario: The promised keyboard equivalence is real
  When a row is reordered using only the keyboard
  Then the move succeeds and the announcement exactly matches the E20-D04 specification

Scenario: Nothing depends on colour
  Given the threshold, provisional and unavailable states rendered in greyscale and under three colour-vision simulations
  Then each remains distinguishable by glyph, word or position

Scenario: The accessible equivalent reaches parity
  When the strip and SCR-045 are compared for the same visible range
  Then every value present in the strip is obtainable from the table

Scenario: The screen reader is not flooded
  Given the forming bar is updating at 4 Hz with default settings
  Then no automatic announcements are produced
```

Manual passes are recorded (screen + audio) and the recordings linked from the ticket, so a disputed finding can be re-examined without re-running the session. Each finding cites the specific WCAG 2.2 success criterion, not a general complaint, so the fix has an objective target.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* an audit. The automated portion is wired into CI by the implementing stories; this ticket verifies the CI configuration actually covers all three surfaces in both themes and both densities, which is a common gap.

## Security notes
N/A — no data handling. The audit does confirm that the insufficient-role export state is explained in text, so a viewer using a screen reader understands why the action is unavailable rather than encountering an unexplained disabled control.

This is the accessibility ticket. Sign-off by the accessibility specialist is a gate on the E20 epic DoD ("a11y: WCAG 2.2 AA verified for all new screens/components introduced by this Epic — axe-core CI green plus at least one manual screen-reader pass").

The audit is performed against the shipping build with the real frame budget in force; any a11y remediation proposed must be checked against E20-Q03's benchmark before it is accepted, so the two gates cannot be satisfied in sequence at each other's expense.

Findings and dispositions recorded in `docs/qa/e20-a11y-audit.md` and linked from the epic, so the R5 accessibility epic (E47) inherits a known state rather than re-discovering it.

body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires an **epic-level** regression/exploratory pass, "not just child-ticket QA", before an Epic can be Done. E20's risk is cumulative rather than local: each story passes its own scenarios, and the defect that reaches the trader is the interaction between them — a threshold set that survives a symbol switch but not a template switch, an export that reflects the row order from before the last reorder, a strip that is correct live and stale in replay. This ticket is the pass that goes looking for those, and the formal QA sign-off gate on the epic.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Execute the full `docs/qa/e20-test-plan.md` black-box plan end to end against the release candidate build, recording pass/fail per scenario.
- Execute the exploratory charter sessions from E20-Q01 (2×90 min, session-based), with written debriefs.
- **Cross-story interaction matrix** executed explicitly: configuration × symbol switch × interval switch × bar-type switch × template switch × workspace reload × replay mode × reconnect — asserting the row set, order, thresholds and values all remain coherent through every combination.
- **Correctness sign-off**: confirm E20-T03's parity harness is green on the full reference symbol-day and that its result is reflected in the epic ticket; independently re-check the hand-computed anchor bar from E20-Q01.
- **Gate roll-up**: confirm E20-Q02 (E2E green on both targets), E20-Q03 (all budgets within gate), E20-Q04 (a11y signed off) and E20-X02 (security signed off) are complete, and record the evidence links in one place.
- Assemble the E20 **regression pack** and register it in the R2 regression suite so the strip is protected through R3–R5.
- Defect triage: every open finding against E20 scope dispositioned; zero open P0/P1 is a hard condition of sign-off.
- QA sign-off comment on the E20 epic with pass/fail per epic-level acceptance criterion.

## Out of scope

```gherkin
  Then every scenario has a recorded pass or fail with evidence
  And every failure has a Bug with a priority label linked to E20
```

title: Render the per-bar Deep-Stats strip aligned to the bar grid
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DS-001 — Per-bar statistics strip (Must)**: "As an order-flow trader, I want a numeric strip under the chart with per-bar totals, so that I read the bar without decoding cells." This is the foundation story of E20; every other story in the epic configures, colours, exports or extends what this one draws. The strip lives under **SCR-030 Chart panel** and is implemented as **CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip**. Its rendering strategy is fixed by E20-K01's measurements and recorded in ADR-0016 (E20-T04); its visual and copy specification comes from the E20-D05 handoff pack; its values come exclusively from `GET /market/metrics` (bootstrap) and the `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` WS topic (live tail), both delivered by E20-T02.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip** implemented to its catalogue contract: props `rows: {id,label,unit,value,thresholdState?,sparkline?:number[]}[]`, `alignedToBars: boolean`, `onConfigure`; rendered as a real `<table>` aligned to the bar grid, not canvas.
- Rows rendered for this story's default set: **Total Volume, Bid Volume, Ask Volume, Delta, Max Delta, Min Delta, Delta %, Cumulative Delta, Number of Trades** (the nine rows named in US-DS-001's "Rows rendered" scenario), each reading its registered metric (`bar_volume`, `bar_sell_volume`, `bar_buy_volume`, `delta`, `max_delta`, `min_delta`, `delta_pct`, `cvd`, `bar_trade_count`).
- Alignment: the strip's column positions derive from the chart engine's time-scale projection `x(t)` — the same projection CMP-181 CandleSeries uses — so alignment is exact at every zoom level and does not lag during pan/zoom.
- **Forming bar**: rendered in the provisional style from the handoff pack (non-colour-only), updating from the live tail coalesced to 4 Hz, and replaced by the authoritative value when the bar closes (`confirm: true`).
- **Narrow-bar collapse**: below the bar width named in the E20-D05 measurement contract, rows collapse to the designed compact form and full values remain available in the crosshair readout.
- **Partial-history state**: when the requested range precedes `meta.recording_started_at`, the strip renders the designed partial-history state naming the first available timestamp; uncovered bars render an explicit "no data", never zero (R2 exit criterion #5).
- **Empty/no-recording state** and the strip-hidden case when no rows are enabled (with the restore affordance in the pane menu — the affordance's configuration UI is E20-S02).
- Storybook stories: Default, AllRows, CompactMode, PartialHistory, Empty(no recording), plus the provisional forming-bar state.
- Instrumentation: a named `performance.measure` around the strip update path, surfaced in the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay.

## Out of scope
- SCR-033 configuration modal, row enable/reorder and persistence — **E20-S02**.
- Threshold colouring — **E20-S03**. Sparklines — **E20-S05**.
- Table view and CSV export — **E20-S04**.
- `tape_speed`, `open_interest_delta`, `bar_poc_price`/`bar_vah_price`/`bar_val_price` rows — available once E25/E24/E18 register them; this story renders whatever the registry offers and shows "unavailable" for descriptors the symbol has no source for.
- Any client-side recomputation of a statistic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Rows rendered and aligned
  Given the stats strip is enabled on SCR-030 for BTCUSDT 5m
  Then Total Volume, Bid Volume, Ask Volume, Delta, Max Delta, Min Delta, Delta %, Cumulative Delta and Number of Trades align under each bar
  And the alignment is exact at 3 zoom levels and remains exact during an active pan

Scenario: Live bar is provisional
  Given the current bar has not closed
  Then its values update in real time at up to 4 Hz
  And it is visually distinguished as provisional by a treatment that is not colour alone
  And when the bar closes its values are replaced by the authoritative bar-close values

Scenario: Narrow bars collapse without losing information
  Given bars are narrower than the minimum legible width from the handoff measurement contract
  Then rows collapse to the compact form
  And the full values for the bar under the crosshair are available in the crosshair readout

Scenario: Partial history is named, not faked
  Given the visible range starts before meta.recording_started_at
  Then the partial-history state is shown naming the first available timestamp
  And bars before that timestamp show "no data" rather than 0

Scenario: Frame budget holds
  Given 13 rows enabled and 400 visible bars on the full R2 scene
  When a 60-second pan/zoom capture is profiled
  Then the strip's contribution is <= 1.5 ms per frame at p95
  And the overall frame p95 stays within 16.6 ms

Scenario: The strip is readable without sight
  When a screen-reader user navigates the strip
  Then it is announced as a table with row headers naming each statistic
  And the forming bar's values do not announce automatically unless the user has opted in
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Data flow:** bootstrap the visible range with `GET /market/metrics` (repeatable `metric`, `bar_type`, `param`, `maxItems: 12` — batch requests if more than 12 rows are enabled), then attach to the live tail via the existing `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` subscription. Key WS frames to bars by bar open time, never by array position — `23-ws-protocol.md` warns that `bars` and `footprint` are separate subscriptions with independent sequences, "guaranteed consistent but not synchronised frame-for-frame".
- **Never treat an unconfirmed bar as closed** (`confirm: false`) — this is the documented flicker bug the flag exists to prevent.
- **Rendering strategy** is whichever E20-K01 recommends and ADR-0016 records; the a11y contract (real `<table>`) is non-negotiable and constrains the choice.
- **Recompute cadence:** on bar close and on visible-range change, not per tick (SCR-033 Performance). The 4 Hz live-tail update mutates cell text for the forming bar only.
- Update writes are batched into `requestAnimationFrame` so a burst of WS frames cannot cause layout thrash (E20-K01 question 5).
- All visual values come from tokens per the E20-D05 token map; no raw values.

## Test plan
- Unit (frontend, >=80% coverage): row-to-metric mapping; provisional vs authoritative replacement keyed by bar open time; compact-collapse threshold boundary (just above and just below); "no data" vs zero rendering; unavailable-descriptor handling.

Read-only market data, `marketdata:read`, `scope=none`. No secrets, PII or order surface. Threats considered: none beyond the epic's export path (not in this story). Per the E20-D04 checklist: real `<table>` with row headers naming each statistic; threshold state (when E20-S03 lands) as word plus icon; the forming bar is non-announcing by default with opt-in announcement, mirroring the CMP-226 BarCountdown precedent; the documented "read current bar's stats" keyboard shortcut is implemented; the compact form relocates information to the crosshair readout rather than removing it; focus is never trapped in the strip. axe-core must report zero serious/critical violations.

## Performance notes
Budgets: SCR-033's <=1.5 ms/frame strip cost (the binding one), US-DS-001's <=2 ms/frame NFR, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budget #1 (frame p95 <=16.6 ms), #2 (never below 30 fps) and #3 (WS tick → screen p95 <100 ms, hard gate at R2). Named `performance.measure` around the strip update, exposed in SCR-046's diagnostics overlay as strip frame cost; client-side counter for dropped/malformed frames; the analytics event `chart.deepstats_rows_changed` is emitted by E20-S02, not here.

title: Select, order and persist Deep-Stats rows via SCR-033
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DS-002 — Row selection and ordering (Must)**: "As a trader, I want to choose which rows appear and in what order, so that the strip fits my screen budget." Screen real estate under the chart is scarce and contested; a fixed nine-row strip is a tax on every trader who wants three. This story builds **SCR-033 Deep Stats rows configuration** (modal) and persists the result so a configured chart stays configured. The full selectable catalogue is the 13 rows named in SCR-033 plus any further §7 descriptors available for the symbol.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-033 modal** per the E20-D05 handoff: checkbox list of available rows with drag handles, per-row ordering, compact-mode toggle, and the sparkline N stepper (the stepper is present and persisted here; sparkline *rendering* is E20-S05 and the control is disabled with an explanatory state until then).
- Selectable row catalogue from SCR-033: Total volume, Bid volume, Ask volume, Delta, Max delta, Min delta, Delta %, Cumulative delta, Trade count, Average trade size, Big-trade count, Speed of tape, Imbalance count — each resolved through `MetricRegistry`; rows whose source is unavailable for the symbol render in the designed unavailable state rather than being silently hidden.
- **Keyboard reorder**: `Alt+Up` / `Alt+Down` move the focused row, with the announcement string specified in E20-D04 ("<Row> moved to position N of M").
- **Validation**: at least one row selected, per SCR-033; the "all rows off" path instead hides the strip entirely and leaves the one-click restore affordance in the pane menu (US-DS-002 scenario "All rows off") — these two requirements are reconciled by treating "hide strip" as an explicit action distinct from deselecting the last row, which the modal's validation message states.
- **Persistence**: row set, order, per-row format and compact flag persisted into the chart template (`chart_templates` jsonb config, `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.2) so they travel with the template and are restored on workspace reload; the standalone-pane case uses `layout_panes.pane_kind='deep_stats'`.
- Analytics event `chart.deepstats_rows_changed {rows}` emitted on apply (not per toggle).
- Components used: CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-049 Table, CMP-056 ColumnPicker, CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip.

## Out of scope
- Threshold configuration UI and colouring — **E20-S03** (this story leaves the designed slot for it).
- Sparkline rendering — **E20-S05**.
- Cross-user or cross-device sync beyond what chart templates already provide (E15 owns template sync).
- Creating new metric descriptors.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Toggle rows
  Given Max Delta and Min Delta are enabled
  When I disable them in SCR-033 and apply
  Then those rows disappear from the strip and the strip height shrinks accordingly
  And chart.deepstats_rows_changed is emitted once with the resulting row list

Scenario: Reorder persists
  When I drag Cumulative Delta to the top and apply
  And I reload the workspace
  Then Cumulative Delta is the first row, restored from the chart template

Scenario: Keyboard reorder is equivalent
  Given focus is on the Delta row in SCR-033
  When I press Alt+Up
  Then Delta moves up one position
  And a screen reader announces "Delta moved to position 2 of 9"

Scenario: All rows off hides the strip with a way back
  When I disable every row
  Then the strip hides entirely
  And a one-click restore affordance remains available in the pane menu

Scenario: Unavailable sources are explained, not hidden
  Given the symbol has no open-interest source
  When SCR-033 is opened
  Then the OI-derived row is listed in the unavailable state with an explanation
  And it cannot be enabled

Scenario: Validation is stated in words
  When I attempt to apply a configuration that is not permitted
  Then an inline message states the rule in text
  And focus moves to the control that must change
```

## Technical notes / design
- Configuration is a pure client-side edit applied atomically on "apply"; there is no per-toggle server round trip. Persistence writes the chart template through the existing E15 template API.
- Row identity is the registered metric name (e.g. `bar_sell_volume`), never the UI label — labels are presentation and may be re-worded; persisted configs must survive that.
- Reordering uses a stable list model so the persisted order is an explicit sequence of metric names, not implied by array mutation side effects.
- The "hide strip" vs "no rows selected" distinction is stored as an explicit `visible: boolean` alongside the row list, so a user who hides the strip does not lose their row configuration.
- Compact mode is persisted per template, not per session, so a template opened on a small display behaves the same way every time.

## Test plan
- Unit (>=80%): list model reorder operations; persistence serialisation/deserialisation round-trip including the `visible` flag; unavailable-source resolution; validation rules.
- Component/Storybook: modal default, all-rows, unavailable-row, validation-error and all-off states; interaction tests for drag and for `Alt+Up`/`Alt+Down`.
- Integration: template save/load round trip against a real `chart_templates` row.
- E2E: toggle, reorder, apply, reload workspace, assert restoration; keyboard-only path start to finish with no mouse events.
- A11y: axe-core on SCR-033; manual screen-reader pass verifying the reorder announcement string exactly matches the E20-D04 spec.

## Security notes
Configuration is presentation state only — no secrets, no PII, no account-scoped data. The persisted jsonb is user-supplied structure, so it must be validated on write against a schema (unknown row ids rejected, list length bounded) to prevent a malformed or oversized template from breaking chart load for the owning user or inflating storage. Data classification: internal, presentation state. No step-up authentication required (SR-025 does not engage — this touches no credentials, risk caps or retention).

## Accessibility notes
Per the E20-D04 checklist: every control has an accessible name; drag reorder has the full `Alt+Up`/`Alt+Down` equivalent with the specified announcement; focus is moved to the offending control on validation failure; modal open/close focus management follows CMP-043 Dialog's contract; the unavailable-row state is explained in text, not conveyed by dimming alone; hit targets meet the WCAG 2.2 AA target-size minimum.

## Performance notes
Applying a configuration must not refetch history the client already holds: disabling a row discards presentation only, and enabling a previously-loaded row re-renders from cache. Enabling a row whose metric was never fetched issues exactly one bootstrap request for the visible range. Strip frame cost after any configuration change must remain within the <=1.5 ms/frame budget, which bounds the maximum enabled row count per E20-K01.

## Observability
Analytics `chart.deepstats_rows_changed {rows}` on apply. A warn log server-side if a template is rejected at write-time validation, including which row id failed, so a client-side bug surfaces rather than silently discarding a user's configuration.

title: Threshold highlighting for Deep-Stats values with per-symbol sets
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DS-003 — Threshold colouring for stats (Should)**: "As a trader, I want values above thresholds highlighted, so that significant bars jump out." A strip of nine numbers is only useful if the eye can find the one that matters; thresholds are what turn a data readout into a signal. The story carries a hard constraint in its NFR — **"no colour-only signalling"** — which matches the epic-wide rule and CMP-225's contract that "threshold state is a word plus an icon". The visual language (shade + marker glyph, token pair per status level) is specified by E20-D03 and packaged in E20-D05.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Threshold configuration in **SCR-033**: per-row threshold rules with a numeric bound and a comparison, validated to the documented range (0–100 % for percentage rows per SCR-033's Validation line; absolute bounds for volume/count rows), and an on/off switch for the whole threshold set.
- **Per-symbol threshold sets**: a named set applies to a symbol; switching symbols applies that symbol's set, and the active set is **named in the legend** (US-DS-003 scenario "Per-symbol thresholds").
- Rendering in **CMP-225**: qualifying cells highlighted with **both** a shade and a marker glyph, plus the `thresholdState` prop populated so the accessible name carries the state as a word.
- Disabled state: with thresholds off, all values render in the neutral style.
- Persistence of threshold rules and the per-symbol set assignment into the chart template alongside the row configuration from E20-S02.
- Storybook state `ThresholdsBreached` (already declared in the CMP-225 catalogue entry) implemented.

## Out of scope
- Alerting or rule creation from a threshold breach (E40 / E35) — a breach is visual only; it fires no notification.
- Threshold-based highlighting anywhere other than the Deep-Stats strip (footprint imbalance highlighting is E18's).
- Auto-suggested thresholds from historical distribution — explicitly deferred; thresholds are user-set in v1.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Strong delta is highlighted in two channels
  Given the strong threshold is Delta % > 60
  When a bar closes with Delta % of 72
  Then that cell is highlighted with both a shade and a marker glyph
  And its accessible name includes the threshold state as a word

Scenario: Per-symbol thresholds
  Given a threshold set is configured for BTCUSDT and a different set for ETHUSDT
  When I switch the chart to ETHUSDT
  Then the ETHUSDT set is applied
  And the active set is named in the legend

Scenario: Disabled
  When thresholds are switched off
  Then all values render in the neutral style
  And no marker glyphs are present

Scenario: Invalid threshold is refused in words
  When I enter 140 as a Delta % threshold
  Then an inline message states that the threshold must be between 0 and 100 %
  And the configuration cannot be applied until it is corrected

Scenario: Greyscale survivability
  Given a breached configuration rendered in greyscale
  Then breached values remain identifiable by glyph and by their accessible name
```

## Technical notes / design
- Threshold evaluation happens at render time against values already received; no server round trip and no additional computation of the underlying statistic.
- Rules are stored as `{metric, comparison, value}` triples keyed by metric name (not label), inside the same chart-template jsonb as the row configuration, under a per-symbol map plus a default set. Symbols with no set fall back to the default rather than to "no thresholds", so a newly opened symbol is not silently unhighlighted.
- Comparison set is deliberately small (`>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `abs >`) — `abs >` exists because delta thresholds are usually magnitude-based regardless of sign, and without it every user would need two mirrored rules.
- Token pairs for the status levels come from `color.status.*` per CMP-225; the glyph is part of the token pair, not chosen at the call site, so the "never colour alone" rule cannot be bypassed by a future caller.

## Test plan
- Unit (>=80%): rule evaluation per comparison including boundary equality; per-symbol set resolution including the default fallback; validation range enforcement; `thresholdState` derivation.
- Component/Storybook: `ThresholdsBreached`, thresholds-off, invalid-input states; a greyscale visual-regression snapshot asserting distinguishability without colour.
- E2E: configure a threshold, observe a breach on a recorded fixture bar known to exceed it, switch symbols and observe the other set applied and named in the legend.
- A11y: axe-core; automated assertion that every breached cell's accessible name contains the state word; manual screen-reader spot-check.
- Contrast: automated check that the shade tokens meet AA against the strip background in both themes.

## Security notes
Presentation-only feature over market data; no secrets, PII or account-scoped data. The persisted rule structure is user-supplied and validated on write (known metric names, bounded rule count, numeric bounds) for the same reasons as E20-S02's row configuration. No new network surface. Data classification: internal, presentation state.

## Accessibility notes
The binding rule is US-DS-003's NFR and CMP-225's contract: **never colour alone**. Every breached value carries a glyph and a word in its accessible name. The legend names the active threshold set in text. Contrast of shade tokens verified in light and dark at both densities. The greyscale visual-regression snapshot is the automated guard that a future styling change cannot quietly reduce this to colour-only.

## Performance notes
Threshold evaluation is O(visible bars × enabled rows) per render and must stay inside the strip's existing <=1.5 ms/frame budget — it adds no new fetch and no new computation of underlying values. The benchmark in E20-Q03 runs with thresholds enabled so the budget is measured in the configuration users will actually run.

## Observability
Threshold configuration changes ride the existing `chart.deepstats_rows_changed` analytics event payload (the event carries the full row configuration, of which thresholds are part), avoiding a second event for the same user action.
