title: Accessible stats table and chunked CSV export of the visible range
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DS-005 — Stats export and accessibility table (Should)**: "As a viewer/analyst, I want the stats strip as an accessible table I can export, so that I can analyse outside the chart." This story serves two audiences with one surface. **SCR-045 Chart data-table alternative** is described in the screens catalogue as "the normative accessible equivalent of SCR-030" that "must reach feature parity for reading data" — so this is not a nice-to-have panel, it is the a11y contract for the whole chart. And the same grid is where CSV export lives, which is where E20's only real security surface sits: exports must be role-scoped, watermarked and audited (SR-098).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Deep-Stats columns added to **SCR-045**'s virtualised grid alongside the existing time/OHLC/volume/delta/CVD columns, respecting the user's enabled row set and order from E20-S02, with the column picker (CMP-056) able to widen beyond it.
- Full keyboard navigation per SCR-045's interaction spec (arrow keys move, `Enter` expands a bar, `Ctrl+C` copies selection as TSV) extended to the Deep-Stats columns.
- **CSV export of the visible range**: one row per bar, one column per enabled statistic, **ISO-8601 UTC timestamps** (US-DS-005 scenario "Export CSV").
- **Chunked export with progress and cancel** for large ranges: ranges above the documented threshold (the story names 50 000 bars) run as an asynchronous job polled via `GET /jobs/{id}`, with visible progress and a working cancel that stops server-side work, not just the UI.
- **Role scoping**: "export respects the user's role; viewers may export only what they can see" (US-DS-005 NFR) — enforced server-side, with the UI rendering the designed insufficient-role state rather than offering an action that will fail.
- **Watermark and audit**: the exported file carries the exporting identity and timestamp, and the export is audited (SR-098).
- Components: CMP-049 Table, CMP-053 Pagination, CMP-056 ColumnPicker, CMP-099 PrintExportBar, CMP-225.
- Analytics: `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported`.

## Out of scope
- Exporting footprint cells or OHLC beyond what SCR-045 already offers (the existing columns are E11/E12's; this story adds the Deep-Stats columns and the CSV path for them).
- Scheduled or recurring exports; export to formats other than CSV.
- Journal/analytics exports (E41) and audit export (E42), which have their own tickets and stricter step-up requirements.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Accessible table
  When I open the table view of the strip with Alt+T
  Then all visible bars and rows are presented as a keyboard-navigable, screen-reader-readable grid
  And each Deep-Stats column has a header that names the statistic and its unit

Scenario: Export CSV
  When I export the visible range
  Then a CSV is produced with one row per bar and one column per enabled statistic
  And every timestamp is ISO-8601 in UTC
  And the file carries a watermark naming the exporting identity and the export timestamp

Scenario: Large range is chunked and cancellable
  Given the visible range exceeds 50 000 bars
  When I export
  Then the export runs as a job with visible progress
  And cancelling stops the job server-side and produces no download

Scenario: Role scoping is enforced server-side
  Given a viewer-role session attempts to export data beyond what its role may read
  Then the request is refused by the server
  And the UI had already rendered the export control in its insufficient-role state with an explanation

Scenario: The export is audited
  When any export completes or is cancelled
  Then an audit record exists naming the actor, the symbol, the range, the row set and the outcome

Scenario: Reading parity with the canvas
  When the table view is compared against the strip for the same visible range
  Then every value shown in the strip is present in the table for the same bar
```

## Technical notes / design
- **No filesystem paths anywhere** (SR-097): the download is addressed by job id through the existing `GET /jobs/{id}` polling contract, which already returns `result.download_url` for completed jobs. Path-traversal and symlink-escape tests are mandatory per SR-097 even though this endpoint accepts no path — the test asserts the absence of the capability.
- The synchronous path (below the chunking threshold) streams the CSV; the asynchronous path reuses the existing job kind machinery rather than inventing a bespoke progress channel.
- CSV formatting: RFC 4180 quoting, `.` decimal separator, no thousands separators, the metric's registered unit named in the header (e.g. `delta (qty)`), and a header comment block carrying the watermark, symbol, bar type, param and generation timestamp.
- Cancellation is cooperative and checked between chunks; a cancelled job leaves no partial artefact reachable by the download URL.
- The table reads the same in-memory series as the canvas (SCR-045 Performance: "no extra fetch is issued") for the visible range; the export path, which may exceed what is in memory, reads server-side.

## Test plan
- Unit (>=80% frontend, >=85% backend export module): CSV formatting including quoting and negative values; ISO-8601 UTC formatting; chunk boundary arithmetic; cancellation between chunks; watermark composition.
- Contract: job responses validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Integration: export a recorded symbol-day and assert the CSV matches the parity harness values from E20-T03 bar-for-bar — the export must be correct, not merely well-formed.
- Security tests: RBAC negative cases per role; the SR-097 no-paths assertion; an oversized-range request rejected rather than accepted-then-truncated; verification that the audit record is written for success, failure and cancellation.
- E2E: open the table with `Alt+T`, navigate by keyboard only, expand a bar, copy as TSV, export a small range, export a large range and cancel it.
- A11y: axe-core on SCR-045; manual screen-reader pass; verification that the grid reaches reading parity with the canvas.
- Perf: virtualised scroll at 100k rows with <=8 ms scripting per scroll frame (SCR-045 budget).

## Security notes
This is E20's principal security surface. Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, per the E20-X01 STRIDE and reviewed in E20-X02:
- **S4 Information disclosure** — exports scoped by role, watermarked with the exporting identity and timestamp, and audited (**SR-098**). Enforcement is server-side; the UI state is a courtesy, never the control.
- **S3 Elevation/path abuse** — no user-supplied filesystem paths; datasets addressed by job id (**SR-097**), with path-traversal tests mandatory.
- **Denial of service** — unbounded export ranges are the obvious abuse; chunking plus a hard maximum range, plus per-user concurrent-export limits, bound the cost. Rejections are explicit, not silent truncations.
- **SR-158** — security acceptance criteria are present on this ticket because it touches data export.
Data classification: market data (not PII, not secrets), but export volume and attribution still make it auditable. Step-up re-authentication (SR-025) is **not** required — market-data export is not in SR-025's enumerated list — and this is recorded deliberately so a reviewer does not assume an omission.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-045 is the normative accessible equivalent of the chart and "must reach feature parity for reading data; verified in every a11y test pass". Requirements: real grid semantics with headers, full keyboard navigation, `Enter` to expand a bar's cells, `Ctrl+C` TSV copy, focus management when the export job starts and completes (progress announced politely, completion announced with the result), and an export control reachable from the chart panel header rather than buried in settings (SCR-045's design checklist: "equal status verified").

## Performance notes
Virtualised grid: <=8 ms scripting per scroll frame at 100k rows (SCR-045). Export: the synchronous threshold is set so a synchronous export completes within a few seconds; beyond it the job path engages. Export throughput and the chunk size are tuned so a 24-hour 1-minute symbol-day exports well within the job timeout, and memory stays flat (streamed, never materialised whole).

## Observability
Structured logs per export job (job id, actor, symbol, range, bar count, row set, duration, outcome); metrics `deepstats_export_rows_total`, `deepstats_export_failures_total`, export duration histogram, and a concurrent-export gauge; audit event per SR-098; analytics `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario passes via an automated test referencing it.
- [ ] Coverage: >=80% frontend, >=85% on the backend export module.
- [ ] Docs: `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-045 and `22-api-openapi.yaml` updated for the export job; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass; reading-parity check against the canvas recorded.
- [ ] security: SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present; abuse-case checks executed (over-broad range, wrong role, cancellation leaving no artefact) per E20-X02.
- [ ] perf: virtualised-scroll benchmark recorded.
- [ ] design-qa: states built for the E20-D06 sweep, including the insufficient-role state.
- [ ] QA sign-off with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review; feature flag state recorded.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue with 2 approvals including a code owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E20-S01` (the strip's row set and values define the table's columns), `E20-T02` (the serving contracts and window limits), `E20-X02` (the export security review must have defined the role-scoping and abuse cases before the control ships). title: Rolling N-bar sparkline per Deep-Stats row
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DS-004 — Rolling sparkline (Could)**: "As a trader, I want a rolling N-bar sparkline per stats row, so that I see trend in the statistic itself." This is the epic's only **Could** story and is deliberately scheduled to **Backlog**, not into the R2 train: E20's budget is 26 points and the Must/Should stories consume it. It is pulled into a sprint only if E20 finishes early or if E20-D01's research showed unexpectedly strong demand. Scheduling it honestly as Backlog is preferable to committing it and cutting it late, which is exactly the R5 Scope risk the risk register warns about.

The story carries a performance guard in its own acceptance criteria — more than 6 sparkline rows triggers a warning and a fallback — which tells us the authors already expected this to be the most expensive thing in the strip.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Per-row sparkline of the last **N** bar values (default N = 20, configurable via the CMP-008 NumericStepperInput already present in SCR-033 from E20-S02), rendered inside CMP-225 using CMP-024 Sparkline's visual language.
- Window change without refetch: changing N redraws from values the client already holds (US-DS-004 scenario "Window change" — "sparklines redraw from cached values with no refetch").

```gherkin
  Then the Delta row shows a compact sparkline of its last 20 bar values

  And no additional network request is issued

Scenario: Performance guard
  Given more than 6 rows have sparklines enabled
  Then a warning is shown in text
  And rendering falls back to the 3 most recently enabled rows

Scenario: Insufficient history
  Given fewer than N bars are available because recording started recently

Scenario: Budget still holds
  Given the maximum permitted sparkline configuration
  When a 60-second capture is profiled
  Then the strip's frame cost remains within its documented budget
```

- The sparkline window is a ring buffer over values the strip already received; increasing N beyond the buffered history shows what exists and states the shortfall, rather than issuing a fetch mid-interaction.

## Security notes
Presentation-only over data already delivered; no new network surface, no secrets, no PII. The only consideration is resource consumption on the client, which the row cap bounds. Data classification: internal, presentation state.

## Accessibility notes
The sparkline is supplementary to a number that is already announced; it is marked `aria-hidden` so a screen-reader user is not read a meaningless graphic, and no information exists only in the sparkline. title: Implement DeepStatsEngine and register Deep-Stats metric descriptors
body:
## Context
Every Deep-Stats row is defined once, in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 ("Deep Stats rows"), as a `MetricDescriptor` in the `MetricRegistry` — and that section states the invariant the whole epic exists to protect: "the metric values themselves are exactly the descriptors above so a rule, an alert and a Deep-Stats row always read the same number". `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.4 names the producer: `DeepStatsEngine` — "Per-bar totals: total/bid/ask volume, delta, max/min delta path, delta %, CVD, trade count", fed by `FootprintEngine`, emitting `DeepStatsRow`, incremental and checkpointable like every other order-flow engine. This Task builds that engine and registers its descriptors. No UI depends on it yet; every later E20 ticket does.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Module `M9` (`orderflow`): `DeepStatsEngine`, consuming `FootprintUpdate` from `FootprintEngine` plus the per-trade stream for the in-progress bar, emitting `DeepStatsRow` events onto the coalescing `of.*` bus.
- Per-bar accumulator state: `buy_volume`, `sell_volume`, notional, trade counts by aggressor, running delta with `max_delta`/`min_delta` path tracking, and the bar's tick range.
- Registration in `MetricRegistry` of every §7 Deep-Stats descriptor with the declared attributes (`scope="symbol"`, `cadence="on_trade"`, authoritative recompute `on_bar_close`, `inputs=("trades",)`, `warmup_bars=0`, `deterministic=True`, `confidence="exact"`): `bar_volume`, `bar_notional`, `bar_sell_volume`, `bar_buy_volume`, `delta`, `max_delta`, `min_delta`, `delta_pct`, `bar_delta_divergence`, `cvd`, `cvd_bar_change`, `bar_trade_count`, `bar_avg_trade_size`, `bar_buy_trade_count`, `bar_sell_trade_count`, `bar_volume_imbalance_ratio`, `bar_range_ticks`. Descriptors owned by other engines and merely *referenced* by the strip (`tape_speed` from `TapeSpeedEngine`, `open_interest_delta` from the derivatives path, `bar_poc_price`/`bar_vah_price`/`bar_val_price` from the footprint value-area computation) are **read**, never redefined.
- Checkpointing: engine state serialises and restores so a restart resumes mid-bar without replaying the session (architecture §3.4 requirement for all order-flow engines).
- The CI test required by `24-internal-schemas.md` §12: "every metric named in §7.2.1 exists in `MetricRegistry` with the declared confidence, and every Deep-Stats row label maps to a registered descriptor".
- Prometheus metrics `deepstats_engine_bar_close_duration_seconds`, `deepstats_rows_emitted_total`.

## Out of scope
- Any HTTP or WS surface (E20-T02) and any UI (E20-S01..S05).
- Defining `tape_speed`, `open_interest_delta` or the value-area metrics — owned by E25, E24 and E18 respectively.
- The offline parity harness (E20-T03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every declared row exists exactly once
  When the MetricRegistry coverage test runs
  Then every Deep-Stats row label in 24-internal-schemas.md §7 resolves to exactly one registered MetricDescriptor with the declared confidence
  And no descriptor owned by another engine is re-registered by DeepStatsEngine

Scenario: Values are correct on a golden bar
  Given the recorded BTCUSDT fixture bar with known buy/sell volumes and print counts
  When the bar closes
  Then delta equals buy_volume - sell_volume
  And delta_pct equals delta / max(bar_volume, qty_step) * 100 and is within -100..100
  And bar_avg_trade_size equals bar_volume / max(bar_trade_count, 1)

Scenario: Degenerate bars do not divide by zero
  Given a bar containing zero trades
  When the bar closes
  Then bar_volume, delta and bar_trade_count are 0
  And delta_pct is 0 rather than NaN or an exception
  And bar_avg_trade_size is 0

Scenario: Restart resumes mid-bar
  Given the engine is mid-bar with a partially accumulated delta path
  When its state is checkpointed and the process is restarted from that checkpoint
  Then the resumed max_delta and min_delta equal the pre-restart values
  And the closed bar equals the value produced by an uninterrupted run over the same tape

Scenario: The in-progress bar is provisional
  When the engine emits for a bar that has not closed
  Then the event is flagged provisional
  And the authoritative recompute at bar close replaces it, and is the value persisted
```

## Technical notes / design
- Incremental only: no recompute from history per tick (architecture §3.4). CPU-heavy paths use `numpy` vectorised ops on preallocated arrays, consistent with the other order-flow engines.
- Aggressor convention is fixed and must not be re-derived: per §7, **Bid Volume = `bar_sell_volume`** (volume executed on the bid, aggressive sellers) and **Ask Volume = `bar_buy_volume`** (aggressive buyers). This mapping is the single most likely source of a sign error in the whole epic and gets its own unit test.
- `delta_pct` uses `max(bar_volume, qty_step)` as the denominator — `qty_step` comes from instruments-info, not a hard-coded epsilon.
- `cvd_bar_change` is defined as equal to `delta` and is kept only for row parity (§7); it must be computed as `cvd(close) - cvd(open)` and asserted equal to `delta` in a test, so a future CVD anchor change cannot silently diverge the two rows.
- `cvd` itself is owned by `CvdEngine` (E23) with a resettable anchor; `DeepStatsEngine` reads it rather than maintaining a second running sum.
- Decimal handling follows the existing market-data convention (fixed-point decimals, not float) end to end; float appears only at the presentation edge.

## Test plan
- Unit (target >=90% on the engine module, floor 85%): per-metric golden values; the bid/ask aggressor mapping test; zero-volume, single-print and single-price bars; `delta_pct` clamping at ±100; checkpoint round-trip equality; provisional-then-authoritative replacement.
- Integration: recorded Bybit fixtures — normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol.
- Property test: for any generated trade sequence, `delta == bar_buy_volume - bar_sell_volume` and `bar_volume == bar_buy_volume + bar_sell_volume`.
- Contract: the `MetricRegistry` coverage test (§12) runs in CI and fails the build on drift.
- Perf: engine bar-close duration benchmarked; must not become a contributor to the backend-internal ≤20 ms budget (#6).

## Security notes
Market data only — no PII, no secrets, no order path. Threat surface is limited to resource consumption: the engine must bound per-symbol state so a pathological symbol cannot grow memory without limit (memory ceiling budgets #7/#8). No new external input is accepted. `security` label not required on this Task; it is covered by the epic STRIDE (E20-X01).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend engine, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Bar-close recompute must complete well inside the coalescing window so it never delays fan-out; target p95 <=2 ms per bar close per symbol at 10 symbols (capacity model, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §10). Memory: per-symbol accumulator state is O(1) in trade count, O(rows) in size.

## Observability
Structured log on checkpoint save/restore (symbol, bar open time, state size). Metrics `deepstats_engine_bar_close_duration_seconds` (histogram, labelled by symbol), `deepstats_rows_emitted_total` (counter, labelled provisional/authoritative). A warn-level log when a bar closes with zero trades for a symbol that is supposed to be actively recording, since that usually means an ingestion gap rather than a quiet market.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by the named tests.
- [ ] Coverage >=85% on the touched backend/engine package, no baseline regression.
- [ ] `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 updated if any descriptor attribute shipped differently from the doc.
- [ ] `MetricRegistry` coverage test green in CI.
- [ ] Perf benchmark recorded for bar-close duration.
- [ ] Reviewed by the order-flow code owner; PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E18-T01` (*Implement FootprintEngine native-tick cell aggregation in M9*, Sprint 10) and `E18-T02` (*imbalance, unfinished-auction, POC and value-area algorithms*, Sprint 10) — `DeepStatsEngine` is fed by `FootprintEngine` (`20-architecture.md` §3.4: `FP --> DS`), and the `bar_poc_price` / `bar_vah_price` / `bar_val_price` / `bar_volume_imbalance_ratio` rows read E18-T02's outputs directly.

Scheduled **Sprint 11**, one sprint after both blockers complete, rather than the earlier Sprint 10 placement: E18's own epic window is S10–S11, so an `E18` epic-level blocker on a Sprint-10 ticket would have started this work before its input existed. Naming the two S10 children instead makes the ordering real and satisfies `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 ("sprint within train window and after blockers"). E18's S11 items (S03–S11 display/colouring/settings) are rendering concerns and are **not** inputs here.

Reads `CvdEngine` output (E23, S12) for the `cvd` row; where E23 has not yet landed, the `cvd` and `cvd_bar_change` rows are registered but return `unavailable` rather than a locally recomputed substitute.

title: Expose Deep-Stats rows over /market/metrics and the footprint WS topic
body:
## Context
The frontend must be able to (a) bootstrap the visible range's statistics over REST and (b) follow the live tail over WS, without inventing a new transport. `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §2 fixes the division: "Bulk history (bars, footprint, profiles, metrics) come from REST; the WS only carries the live tail plus the initial snapshot needed to attach to it." Both surfaces already exist — `GET /market/metrics` takes a repeatable `metric` parameter and returns one series per value with a parameter echo, and the `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` topic already carries per-bar `delta`, `poc_price`, `value_area_high`/`value_area_low` in `FootprintUpdate` (§14.4). This Task wires `DeepStatsEngine`'s output into those two existing contracts and closes the gaps, interface-first (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10) so E20-S01 can start against a merged schema.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /market/metrics`: accept every Deep-Stats metric code registered by E20-T01 in the `MetricCode` enum; serve bar-scoped series honouring `bar_type` + `param`; echo per-metric params; populate `meta.recording_started_at` so the UI can render the partial-history state (R2 exit criterion #5).
- WS: ensure the `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` frames carry the per-bar statistics the strip needs for the live tail, and that the last bar's `confirm: false` flag is present so the client can render it as provisional (§ "Unconfirmed bars" — "A client MUST NOT treat it as closed").
- Schema delta merged into `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and, if any WS field is added, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §14.4 plus the JSON-schema file, **before** implementation.
- Validation and limits: reject windows that exceed the documented cap with the existing `validation_failed` / `footprint_window_too_large` error codes; `maxItems: 12` on the repeated `metric` parameter is enforced, not assumed.
- RBAC: `marketdata:read`, `scope=none`, per the `x-rbac` block on the endpoint and the WS subscription permission table.
- Contract tests asserting response and frame shapes against the committed schemas.

## Out of scope
- The CSV export endpoint and job (E20-S04).
- New metrics (E20-T01) or new transports/encodings.
- Client-side consumption (E20-S01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bootstrap returns every enabled row
  Given a request for metric=bar_volume&metric=delta&metric=delta_pct with bar_type=time and param=5
  When GET /market/metrics is called for a 500-bar window
  Then three series are returned, each with its own params echo and unit
  And meta.recording_started_at is present

Scenario: Too many metrics is rejected cleanly
  Given a request with 13 repeated metric parameters
  Then the response is 400 with validation_failed and names the maxItems limit
  And no partial series are returned

Scenario: Window too large is rejected with the documented code
  Given a window exceeding the documented footprint window cap
  Then the response is 422 with footprint_window_too_large
  And the message states the maximum window

Scenario: The live tail marks the forming bar
  Given a subscription to footprint.BTCUSDT.time.5
  When a frame arrives containing the currently forming bar
  Then that bar carries confirm: false
```

title: Golden-fixture parity harness: strip values vs offline DuckDB recompute
body:
## Context
R2 exit criterion #6 is explicit: "Footprint, profile, CVD and Deep-Stats values match an independent offline recomputation (DuckDB over the Parquet tier) for a full recorded symbol-day, within floating-point tolerance." The R2 quality-gate table reinforces it: "Golden-fixture tests: one recorded symbol-day with expected footprint/profile/CVD/Deep-Stats outputs version-controlled; any drift fails CI". This Task builds E20's half of that harness. It is the single strongest defence against the epic's headline risk (R7 Data accuracy): a strip that is beautiful, fast, accessible and **wrong** is worse than no strip, because the trader will act on it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- An independent recomputation of every Deep-Stats row in SQL over the Parquet cold tier via DuckDB, using the documented views (`21-database-schema.md` §cold tier: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW footprint_cells AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet(...)` and the equivalent trades view). **Independent** means written from the definitions in `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 by someone not implementing `DeepStatsEngine`, not a port of the engine code — a shared bug would otherwise pass silently.
- A version-controlled golden fixture: one full recorded symbol-day (BTCUSDT, the R2 reference day) with expected per-bar values for every row, stored under `tests/fixtures/e20/` with a documented provenance record (symbol, date, recording session id, bar type, param, tick size, `qty_step`).
- A CI job comparing engine output against the golden fixture bar-for-bar with a documented floating-point tolerance, failing the build on drift and reporting the first N divergent bars with both values.
- A comparison of the three serving tiers (engine hot state, QuestDB warm, Parquet cold) so a value does not change depending on where it was read from.
- A regeneration script with a deliberate guard: regenerating the golden fixture requires an explicit flag and produces a diff summary for review, so a real regression cannot be laundered into a "fixture update".

## Out of scope
- Footprint, profile and CVD golden fixtures (E18, E19, E23 own theirs; this harness shares their fixture day and infrastructure where it already exists).
- Frontend rendering correctness (E20-Q02 covers that at the E2E layer).
- Performance measurement (E20-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A full symbol-day agrees
  Given the recorded BTCUSDT reference day
  When the engine output and the DuckDB recomputation are compared for every bar and every Deep-Stats row
  Then 100% of values agree within the documented tolerance

Scenario: Drift fails the build
  Given a deliberately introduced sign error in the aggressor mapping
  When the CI parity job runs
  Then the job fails and names the affected metric and the first divergent bar with both values

Scenario: All three tiers agree
  Given the same 500-bar window is served from engine state, from QuestDB and from the Parquet tier
  Then the Deep-Stats values are identical across the three

Scenario: Fixture updates are deliberate
  When the golden fixture is regenerated without the explicit regeneration flag
  Then the script refuses and prints the diff summary instead of overwriting
```

## Technical notes / design
- Tolerance is documented per metric family, not global: exact equality for counts (`bar_trade_count`, `bar_buy_trade_count`, `bar_sell_trade_count`, `bar_range_ticks`), fixed-point exact for volumes and deltas, and a stated relative tolerance only for ratios (`delta_pct`, `bar_avg_trade_size`, `bar_volume_imbalance_ratio`) where division introduces representation error.
- The reference day must include at least one `recording_gaps` row so the harness proves the "partial history" behaviour rather than only the happy path (`21-database-schema.md`: every query over a range intersecting a gap must render the partial-history state).
- The SQL lives under `tests/parity/e20/*.sql` with one file per metric, each carrying the §7 definition as a comment header so a reviewer can check SQL against spec without opening another document.

## Test plan
This Task *is* test infrastructure. Its own correctness is verified by mutation: a set of seeded faults (aggressor swap, off-by-one bar boundary, wrong `qty_step` in the `delta_pct` denominator, dropped final trade of a bar) must each be caught by the harness; a fault that passes is a harness bug. Runtime target: the full-day parity job completes in <=10 minutes so it can run on every PR touching M9.

## Security notes
The harness reads recorded market data only. The fixture must be checked for accidental inclusion of account-identifying data before being committed (the recorded tape is public market data, but the provenance record must not embed a recording session's account context). Fixture files are committed with Git LFS if they exceed the repository size policy.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Parity job runtime <=10 minutes on CI hardware; it runs on PRs touching M9 and nightly on `main`. The DuckDB recomputation reads the Parquet tier directly and must not query QuestDB, so it cannot be slowed by, or interfere with, live ingestion.

## Observability
CI job emits a structured summary (rows compared, metrics compared, max observed deviation per metric) retained as a build artefact, so a slow drift toward the tolerance edge is visible before it becomes a failure.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified, including the seeded-fault mutation set.
- [ ] Golden fixture and provenance record committed; regeneration guard in place.
- [ ] CI job wired to PRs touching M9 and to the nightly build; runtime within budget.
- [ ] `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` updated with the parity harness entry if it establishes a new pattern.
- [ ] Reviewed by QA/SDET and the order-flow code owner; PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E20-T01` (there must be engine output to compare against) and `E20-T02` (the harness compares the **served** payload, not just in-process engine state). Moved to Sprint 12 to stay after T01's corrected Sprint-11 placement. title: STRIDE threat model for the Deep-Stats epic

## Context
`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` makes a STRIDE threat model mandatory per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the kickoff to be scheduled before an Epic enters Ready. E20's surface looks benign — market data, read-only, no credentials, no order path — and that is precisely why it needs a model rather than an assumption: the epic ships a **data export** (SR-098 territory), an **asynchronous job with a download URL** (SR-097 territory), and a **user-supplied persisted configuration structure**. `04-security-program.md` already records S3 (elevation of privilege: "Replay/export endpoint used to read arbitrary filesystem paths", rated High) and S4 (information disclosure via export) as programme-level threats; this model determines how they apply here and what E20-T02, E20-S02 and E20-S04 must implement.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Data-flow diagram (mermaid) covering: Bybit tape → ingestion → `FootprintEngine` → `DeepStatsEngine` → bus → WS fan-out → client strip; and the REST paths `GET /market/metrics`, `GET /market/footprint`, the export job and `GET /jobs/{id}` → download.
- Trust boundaries marked: exchange↔ingestion, backend↔client (over Tailscale only), and the role boundary between Owner/Manager/Viewer.
- Per-category analysis with at least one concrete threat each:
  - **Spoofing** — can a session subscribe to a topic or call an endpoint without `marketdata:read`?
  - **Tampering** — can a malformed or hostile template configuration (unknown row ids, oversized list, deep nesting) corrupt chart load or inflate storage? Can a malformed WS frame cause the client to render a fabricated value?
  - **Repudiation** — is an export attributable? (SR-098 watermark + audit.)
  - **Information disclosure** — can a Viewer export data beyond its role? Does the export leak account context through the provenance/watermark block?
  - **Denial of service** — unbounded export range, excessive concurrent exports, an over-broad `/market/metrics` window, a row configuration whose render cost breaks the frame budget.
  - **Elevation of privilege** — can the job/download mechanism be coerced into serving another user's artefact or a filesystem path (SR-097)?
- **Abuse cases** written as executable test intents, handed to E20-X02 and E20-Q01.
- Required controls mapped to the tickets that implement them (E20-T02 limits, E20-S02 template validation, E20-S04 role scoping/watermark/audit/cancellation), so no control is identified without an owner.

## Out of scope
- Threat models for E18, E19, E21 or E26 (each owns its own; E26 and E21 are named explicitly in the R2 security gate).
- Penetration testing (R4, E43).
- Implementing the controls.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every STRIDE category is addressed
  When the threat model is reviewed
  Then each of the six categories has at least one identified threat with a likelihood, impact, rating, control and residual risk
  And every control references an SR identifier from 04-security-program.md or states why no existing SR applies

Scenario: Every control has an owning ticket
  When the control table is reviewed
  Then each control names the E20 ticket that implements it
  And no control is left unassigned

Scenario: Abuse cases are testable
  When the abuse-case list is reviewed
  Then each is written so that E20-X02 or E20-Q01 can execute it and observe a pass or fail
```

## Technical notes / design
The model must explicitly record the **negative findings** as well — that E20 touches no credentials, no order path and no PII, and that SR-025 step-up re-authentication therefore does not apply to market-data export. Recording the reasoning prevents a later reviewer from reading the absence of step-up as an oversight, and prevents a well-meaning engineer from adding friction the standard does not require.

## Test plan
N/A (analysis artefact). Verified by the Security engineer's review and by E20-X02 executing the abuse cases against the built surfaces.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security analysis. Its output gates E20-T02 (which must implement the window and cardinality limits the model identifies) and informs E20-S04's export controls. Data classification of the epic is recorded here: market data, internal; no PII; no secrets; export attributable.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The model treats frame-budget exhaustion via a pathological row configuration as a genuine availability threat, not merely a performance concern, and routes it to the row-count guard that E20-K01 sized — which is why the two tickets cross-reference.

## Observability
The model specifies the security-relevant events E20 must emit: export attempted/succeeded/failed/cancelled with actor and range, template-validation rejections, and RBAC refusals on the market-data read path — all of which feed the SR-125 security metrics set.

title: Security review of the Deep-Stats export path and abuse-case testing
body:
## Context
E20's only meaningful security surface is the CSV export introduced by US-DS-005 and built in E20-S04. `04-security-program.md` rates the related programme threats highly: **S3** (elevation of privilege — "Replay/export endpoint used to read arbitrary filesystem paths", High) with control **SR-097** ("Replay, export and import endpoints MUST NOT accept filesystem paths; datasets are addressed by registry ids. Path traversal and symlink escape tests are mandatory"), and **S4** (information disclosure via export) with control **SR-098** ("Exports MUST be role-scoped, watermarked with the exporting identity and timestamp, and audited"). **SR-158** requires security acceptance criteria on every ticket touching data export. This ticket is the white-box review and the executed abuse cases that verify those controls actually hold in the built system, rather than merely appearing in a ticket body.

Note the sequencing: this ticket is scheduled alongside E20-S04 and **blocks** it, because the role-scoping and abuse-case definitions must be settled before the export control ships, not audited after.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box code review** of the export path end to end: request validation, role resolution, range bounding, chunking, cancellation, artefact lifecycle, download URL issuance via `GET /jobs/{id}`, watermark composition, and audit-record emission.
- **Executed abuse cases** from the E20-X01 model, each with recorded evidence:
  1. Viewer-role session attempts an export beyond its role → refused server-side (not merely hidden in the UI).
  2. Manager attempts to retrieve another user's export artefact by job id → refused.
  3. Path traversal and symlink escape attempts against the download mechanism → impossible by construction, asserted by test (SR-097).
  4. Over-broad range request → rejected with an explicit error, not silently truncated.
  5. Many concurrent export requests from one session → bounded by the documented concurrency limit; the service remains responsive.
  6. Cancel mid-export then attempt to download → no artefact reachable, and the cancellation is audited.
  7. Hostile chart-template payload (unknown row ids, oversized row list, deeply nested jsonb) → rejected at write-time validation without breaking chart load for the user (tampering case from E20-X01).
  8. Malformed WS footprint frame → dropped and surfaced as stale data; no fabricated value rendered.
- **Verification of the audit trail**: each export attempt produces a record naming actor, symbol, range, row set and outcome; records are append-only and survive the retention policy.
- **Watermark verification**: the exported file carries the exporting identity and timestamp in a form that survives opening in a spreadsheet application (a watermark only visible in a hex editor is not a control).
- **SAST/DAST/SCA confirmation** for the touched code: Semgrep/Bandit rules green or triaged, `pip-audit`/`npm audit` clean or triaged, and a ZAP pass over the new endpoint; a Semgrep rule added if the review finds a pattern worth preventing programme-wide.
- Findings triaged: fixed, or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off recorded.

## Out of scope
- The threat model itself (E20-X01).
- Penetration testing (R4, E43) and audit-log infrastructure (E42).
- Security review of footprint, profiles, DOM ladder or replay (each owns its own; the R2 security gate names E26 and E21 specifically).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Role scoping is enforced where it counts
  Given a viewer-role session with the UI control bypassed
  When it calls the export endpoint directly for data beyond its role
  Then the server refuses the request
  And the refusal is audited

Scenario: No path reaches the filesystem
  When the download mechanism is reviewed and tested with traversal and symlink payloads
  Then no user-supplied value reaches a filesystem path
  And the SR-097 mandatory traversal and symlink tests are present and passing

Scenario: Exports are attributable
  When any export completes
  Then the file carries the exporting identity and timestamp legibly when opened in a spreadsheet application
  And an append-only audit record exists naming actor, symbol, range, row set and outcome

Scenario: Resource abuse is bounded
  Given repeated over-broad and concurrent export requests
  Then each over-broad request is rejected with an explicit error
  And concurrency is bounded by the documented limit with the service remaining responsive

Scenario: Cancellation leaves nothing behind
  When an export is cancelled mid-run
  Then no artefact is reachable by its job id
  And the cancellation is audited

Scenario: Hostile configuration is rejected safely
  When a template with unknown row ids and an oversized row list is written
  Then the write is rejected with a validation error
  And the user's existing chart configuration still loads
```

## Technical notes / design
- The review must confirm enforcement is **server-side**: a UI that hides the export control is a usability feature, never a security control, and the review explicitly tests with the UI bypassed.
- Artefact lifecycle: download URLs should be single-purpose and expiring; the review records the chosen lifetime and whether it is enforced.
- The watermark is a header comment block in the CSV; the review confirms it survives a spreadsheet round trip rather than being silently stripped.

## Test plan
- Security integration tests committed alongside the findings so each abuse case becomes a permanent regression test, not a one-off manual check.
- SR-097's traversal/symlink tests are mandatory and must exist even though the endpoint accepts no path — they assert the absence of the capability.
- RBAC negative tests per role for both the export endpoint and the market-data read path.
- SAST/SCA/DAST evidence attached to the ticket.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security review, required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 for any ticket carrying the `security` label and by SR-158 for anything touching data export. Data classification: market data, internal — but attributable and audited on export. Step-up re-authentication (SR-025) is confirmed as not applicable and the reasoning is recorded, consistent with E20-X01's negative findings.

## Accessibility notes
Confirms that the insufficient-role state is explained in text so the security control degrades accessibly — a user who cannot export learns why rather than encountering an unexplained disabled control.

## Performance notes
The concurrency and range limits are set with reference to the export throughput measured in E20-S04, so the bound is protective rather than arbitrary; the review records the numbers.

## Observability
Verifies the SR-125-relevant events are emitted and alertable: RBAC refusals on the market-data path, export failures, template-validation rejections, and export concurrency at the limit.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] White-box review completed with notes recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] All eight abuse cases executed with evidence; each converted into a committed regression test.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/DAST results clean or triaged with dispositions.
- [ ] All findings fixed, or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off recorded.
